sections.title: The new upscaler is generative — and Anlas is not usage
sections.lede: Model-independent. Grainy vs smooth regions. Paid Anlas upscale does not eat your allotment.
sections.body:
Friday already taught that the upscaler is unrelated to V5. This window filled in the product facts. luna: the new upscaler is model independent and does not apply to usage. mahouko: it is generative — a system that classifies regions as grainy or smooth and applies different strategies to each. finetune: if you pay Anlas for it, that spend does not count toward usage. Stop treating upscale as a V5-only dial or as a free meter burn.

**Try this.** Take one keeper you already like. Same seed family, V5 Full, Euler/karras, guidance 5, 23 steps, QT on, rescale 0. Generate at native size (A). Upscale via the product upscaler (B). Compare grainy vs smooth regions — do not chase bit-identical restores. Note Anlas cost separately from daily usage.

**CTA.** Guren: one A/B upscale pair. Ivory: file whether Studio presets still imply upscale = V5. Do not invent PE() contract changes — contracts were not re-dumped.

sections.title: Underscore strip is finetune — prefer spaced tags
sections.lede: It is not frontend. Do not rely on auto-strip. Intentional underscore exceptions exist.
sections.body:
mahouko guessed underscores become spaces. ght901 corrected the mechanism: that strip is finetune, not frontend behaviour. It attempts to remove underscores to save you from yourself, but it should not be relied on — edge cases remain. Prefer tags without underscores (intentional underscore keepers excepted). Uchariko showed a live mismatch: `careena_(visions_of_mana)` vs `careena (visions of mana)` come out different in the main prompt (same in character prompt). Low model understanding of the character amplifies the gap for copyrighted name tags.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler, guidance 5, QT on. A: main prompt with underscore form `1girl, careena_(visions_of_mana), looking at viewer`. B: spaced `1girl, careena (visions of mana), looking at viewer`. Compare identity, then move both forms into the character box and re-run.

**CTA.** Ivory: audit Studio presets that still ship underscore danbooru pastes. Rewrite to spaced tags.

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: no, that'd be finetune. It's not frontend behaviour. It attempts to remove the underscores from tags as a way to save you from yourself but it shouldn't be relied on. There's likely edge cases where it doesn't remove things when it arguably should. You should be using tags without underscores (the ones where it's intentionally left in excepted)

excerpts.speaker: mahouko
excerpts.text: probably tags with underscores get transformed into spaces

excerpts.speaker: Uchariko
excerpts.text: So I agree with Guns and it works as expected when in the character prompt (i.e., they're the same), but why is it that if I put `careena_(visions_of_mana)`/`careena (visions of mana)` in the main prompt, they come out different? I'll note that other characters with `(<copyright>)`s in their tag also come out different to much lesser extents and the larger difference for `careena (visions of mana)` is probably because of low model understanding of the character

sections.title: Precise height measurements are useless here
sections.lede: Hex colors (maybe) are not a license for numeric cm/ft heights.
sections.body:
Someone hoped the model would honor precise height measurements the way people claim hex colors work. ght901 shut both halves down on nai-image-advice: do not expect anything useful from precise height numbers, and even if hex colors work reliably, that is an entirely different thing — there is no reason to believe the model will understand numeric heights from that. Shipping `165cm` / `5'4"` as tags is cargo-cult. Describe relative size in natural language (`taller than`, `shorter than`, `towering over`, `looking up at`) and let composition do the rest.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler/karras, guidance 5–6, 23 steps, QT on, rescale 0. Two-girl scene. A: `1girl is 165cm, 1girl is 180cm, standing together`. B: `the brown-haired girl is shorter than the white-haired girl, looking up at her, standing together`. Compare height signal and eye-line, not vibes.

**CTA.** Guren: one A/B. If A fails, delete numeric heights from any living preset and `save_memory` the relational NL form only if pixels agree.

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: I would not expect the model to get anything useful out of heights given in precise measurements and you probably shouldn't expect it to either

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: even if hex colors do work reliably, no, that's an entirely different thing and there's no reason to believe from that that the model will understand precise height measurements

sections.title: Vibe is conditioning, not a LoRA
sections.lede: Staff correction when users analogize NovelAI vibe transfer to PixAI LoRA/reference.
sections.body:
Room chatter kept treating vibe transfer like a portable LoRA or PixAI-style reference adapter. mahouko cut it flat on nai-diffusion-discussion: it is not related to LoRA in any way; it is just conditioning. That changes how you debug failures — do not expect LoRA-style stacking, merge math, or reference-slot habits to port. Treat vibe as conditioning strength on the current image path, and stop blaming "missing LoRA slots" when a vibe drifts composition.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler, guidance 5, 23 steps, QT on. A: no vibe. B: one vibe transfer at moderate strength. C: crank strength. Watch composition drift vs style paste. Do not add a second vibe as if it were a LoRA slot.

**CTA.** Ivory: note Studio copy that still says vibe≈LoRA and correct the language. Guren: one ladder only — stop when battery thins.

excerpts.text: it’s not related to LoRA in any way; it’s just conditioning

Uchariko posted a clean three-character recipe: prose the dance/flute scene in the base prompt, then reinforce each concept inside character boxes — including `mutual#dancing` on the pair that should share the action. Prose alone is not enough for reliability on multi-character work. Label stays ANECDOTE until a second independent voice repeats it.

Base: `2girls, 1boy, year 2025, very aesthetic, masterpiece, no text. the brown-haired girl and the boy are dancing together. the red-haired girl is playing the flute.` Boxes: `girl, brown hair, red dress, mutual#dancing, smile, hand on another's shoulder | boy, white hair, short hair, brown pants, white shirt, mutual#dancing, smile | girl, red hair, green tunic, holding flute`. A: with mutual# in boxes. B: prose only, boxes identity-only. Compare action binding.

**CTA.** Guren: run A/B once. If A wins, `save_memory` the mutual# pattern — still ANECDOTE, not CONSENSUS.

sections.body:
On danbooru, multiple artist tags often co-occur with `artist collaboration` — different styles per character, extra faces in the background. Uragan says 4.5 needed a strong negative for artist mixes and V5 still does: put `-6::artist collaboration::` in the main prompt to fuse character styles and reduce stray bg faces when you stack many artist tags. This is community advice, not Anlatan staff. Keep [ANECDOTE] until staff or a second independent repeat confirms.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler, guidance 5. Six-artist mix in base. A: no collaboration neg. B: add `-6::artist collaboration::`. Count bg faces and style split across characters.

**CTA.** Guren: one six-artist A/B. Ivory: do not promote to CONSENSUS from one voice.

excerpts.speaker: Uragan
excerpts.text: 4.5 needed it when you used artist mixes, and it still does now. On danbooru, when there's multiple artist tags on a picture, there's also the tag `artist collaboration`, it means more than one artist participated, and most of the time, they make characters with their own styles, making a difference in style between characters, which is not what we want. Adding it in negative fuses the character styles, and also prevent faces in the background from appearing (if you use 6 artist tags, but only h

excerpts.speaker: Uragan
excerpts.text: Put `-6::artist collaboration::` in your main prompt. That's your solution.

sections.lede: Uragan: −6::artist collaboration:: fuses styles and cuts background faces. Not STAFF.
sections.title: artist collaboration neg still recommended on V5 mixes

sections.body:
Artist-mix NL lines can silently break when a name that starts with digits sits next to `::`. AmbiProp flagged a live stack on nai-image-advice: in `drawn by the following artists:  0.5::sakimichan::, brian froud, 1.1::hobbyr34::, 0.8::naohiro ito::,` the `hobbyr34` sitting next to `::` turns into a multiplier. Keep spaces and structure clean — do not glue bare digits against emphasis delimiters after a close. This is ANECDOTE (one clear repro voice); still worth linting every artist mix.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler, guidance 5, QT on. A: the broken line above. B: insert spaces / rename the artist token so a digit never touches `::` after a close. Compare style strength on the hobbyr34 slot.

**CTA.** Ivory: lint Studio artist stacks for digit-glued `::`. Guren: optional one-seed check.

sections.body:
On unofficial nai-image-gen-discussion, Kirari~n, OccultSage, and matts7123 lined up against defaulting many tags to `5::`. OccultSage: barely uses emphasis; `5::` is really high — a sledgehammer. matts7123: high positive emphasis for specific hard effects (even `6::` once), never every tag; when blending anime and photoreal, weaken photo and strengthen anime selectively. Stays [UNOFFICIAL] even though the room agrees — do not promote to CONSENSUS from unofficial-only repeats.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler, guidance 5. Take a fried preset that wraps half its tags in `5::`. A: as-is. B: strip to plain tags + selective `1.1::`–`1.5::` on the one failing concept. Compare fry vs control.

**CTA.** Guren: one strip test. Do not `save_memory` a universal 5:: ban — report the before/after.

excerpts.speaker: Kirari~n ☆
excerpts.text: I still maintain that you'd have a lot less issues making things look right if you didn't default to 5:: emphasis for half your tags

excerpts.speaker: OccultSage [+7 WIS]
excerpts.text: Wow. I barely even use emphasis. 5:: is really really high, and like applying a sledgehammer.

excerpts.speaker: matts7123
excerpts.text: I've had to put high positive emphasis on some things, but never every tag. I've had to go to 6:: for some specific things to get the effect i wanted. When I was testing blending anime and photo realistic, I had to both weaken photo  realistic and strengthen anime.

**Workspace:** Laboratory (`516399f0-bb42-4e84-8149-11f6ba1d61d8`) only — not Default.

**Anlas ≠ usage (from pixels + tool):** Three paid `upscale_image` (novelai 2x) runs succeeded with `allow_paid` / `userApprovedPaidRequest`. Responses returned `upscaled:true`, `upscaler_provider:novelai`, `upscale_ratio:2`, actual size **1664×2432** — and **no Anlas / cost / usage fields**. Schema labels the gate "Paid Opus." Daily Opus usage meter is a different ledger; do not invent Anlas balances from a missing field.

**3 A/B pairs (keepers = Laboratory):**
1. **Careena** seed 2026091401 — A `1789420525301_generated_2026091401.png` → B `1789420525301_generated_2026091401_upscaled.png`. White BG stays clean; B sharpens hair tips + frill scallops; skin stays smooth. Generative, not bit-identical.
2. **Height NL** seed 2026091411 — A `1789420536581_generated_2026091411.png` → B `1789420536581_generated_2026091411_upscaled.png`. B smooths shirt/skin flats, clarifies silver hair strands + bag charms; foliage less muddy.
3. **Artist-collab neg** seed 2026091441 — A `1789420557136_generated_2026091441.png` → B `1789420557136_generated_2026091441_upscaled.png`. B smooths sweater grain, clarifies hydrangea petals + ahoge wisps.

**Accidental Default burns (ignore):** `1789396519418_…_upscaled.png`, `1789396619513_…_upscaled.png`, `1789396764163_…_upscaled.png` — early wrong-workspace run.

**Try this:** Pick a Laboratory native keeper → `upscale_image` with `upscaler:"novelai"`, `workspace` Laboratory, `allow_paid:true` only after Yukimi green-light. Compare grainy (hair edges, foliage, dark fabric) vs smooth (skin, flat whites) — do not chase pixel-identical restores.

**CTA:** Next paid pass — expand A/B or vibes once a Studio client is bound. Keep all Try-this in Laboratory.
